subject: Money
title: Sin Taxes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sin Taxes.

hook.text: A pack of cigarettes costs $14 in New York. About $6 is the product. The rest is tax.

buildup.text: Sin taxes target goods society wants to discourage: tobacco, alcohol, sugary drinks, gambling.

discovery.text: They serve two goals: raise revenue and reduce harmful behavior. Price people out of bad habits.

twist.text: Sin taxes are regressive. Low-income people smoke more and spend a larger share of income on these taxes.

climax.text: Governments depend on the revenue they're trying to reduce. If everyone quits, the money disappears.

punchline.text: Tax the sin. Fund the budget. Hope nobody quits.

quiz.question: What's the paradox of sin taxes?
options: Governments depend on revenue from behavior they discourage
